title: Nonregular Minimax Rates for a Latent Fourier Treatment Contrast under Triangular Error
banked_reason: The delivered result characterizes one fixed cosine contrast under one exactly known triangular error law and a supplied tail exponent; this is a specialized technical contribution below the field-tier floor.

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived matched MSE and connected honest-interval-length rates uniformly over known q in [2,5], including the critical logarithm and moving-q transition, then enlarged the result to the anchor published Lipschitz and upper-tail class. Mathematics and decision panels passed and six source leaves were independently attested; the typed novelty and projected-paper-score gate nevertheless capped this fixed triangular-noise functional contribution at incremental below the field floor. No Lean formalization was entered; an arbitrary compact-supported double-zero noise family is a future proposal re-anchor, not an unfinished same-scope fix.
tldr: On the published Goldenshluger--Kim H\"older-one class with only a one-sided density upper tail, one noisy outcome per randomized subject suffices to estimate the bounded latent cosine treatment contrast. Triangular error annihilates its reported-outcome coordinate. The full-class MSE is comparable to \(r_n(q)=n^{-1}V_q((n+1)^{1/(q+3)})\), and the minimax expected length of connected uniformly \(90\%\)-honest intervals is comparable to \(\sqrt{r_n(q)}\), uniformly for public \(q\in[2,5]\). A smooth cutoff score and public bias-aware interval attain these orders. Exactly mass-zero packets give legal positive heavy-tail witnesses and the critical multiscale logarithm. The lower envelope is a proved witness property, not a class assumption; the two-arm embedding itself adds no novelty.
gap: Existing zero-aware density bounds and regular inverse-information theory do not determine the nonregular accuracy of this bounded coordinate on the stated primitive density class.
fill: A computable finite-sample honest procedure and all-procedure converse determine the precision of one calibrated latent distributional-treatment-effect coordinate.
